Mizzou Neuroscience
Shaping the Future of Neuroscience Research
Join an active community of faculty and graduate students from a wide range of disciplines, all engaged in pioneering basic and clinical research on the molecular and cellular organization of the nervous system, the function of crucial neural system, complex brain-generated behaviors, and the challenges of neurological diseases and disorders.
A Dynamic and Exciting Field of Graduate Study
The field of neuroscience is a vibrant tapestry, weaving together insights from biology, psychology, computer science, engineering, and neurology, among many others. Mizzou’s neuroscience graduate program embodies this interdisciplinary spirit.
The strength of our graduate program lies in the combined expertise of the 40+ research-active faculty who comprise the Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program (INP). Whether your interests lie in investigating the molecular and cellular intricacies of the nervous system, the functionality of crucial neural pathways, complex brain-driven behaviors, or creating innovative therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, the INP will provide you with the academic, research, and technological resources you need to succeed.
Explore our Faculty Directory
Degrees Offered
We are committed to providing a broad yet individualized training experience to prepare our graduates to succeed in future careers in academic research and teaching institutions, industry, and scientific publication.
Graduate Certificate
We provide a Graduate Certificate in Neuroscience to current MU post-baccalaureate and non-INP graduate students enrolled in neuroscience courses and research labs. This stand-alone certificate is aimed at students interested in applying to graduate or professional school or a career in industry.
Graduate Degrees
We offer graduate work leading to the degrees of Master of Science (MS) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) with a current enrollment of about 30 graduate students. The graduate studies program is interdisciplinary and highly individualized.

Research Highlights
Mizzou’s large and multidisciplinary neuroscience community is dedicated to pushing the frontiers of research. These efforts accelerate vital breakthroughs and inspire innovative, collaborative approaches to both teaching and discovery.
